title: Multiples, Factors, Prime Factorisation, HCF and LCM
seo_title: Grade 7 Multiples, Factors and Primes Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Multiples and factors: list prime factors of numbers to at least 3-digit whole numbers; find the LCM and HCF of numbers to at least 3-digit whole numbers, by inspection or factorisation.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 7 worksheets: factors, multiples, primes, prime factorisation, index notation, HCF and LCM. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: HCF: shared primes. LCM: all primes, most times.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 1 is not prime.
  • Prime factorisation writes a number as a product of primes: 360 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 2³ × 3² × 5.
  • HCF: multiply the prime factors the numbers share. LCM: use every prime factor the most times it appears.
  • A factor tree helps you find the prime factors.

Examples

Example

HCF and LCM of 24 and 36

24 = 2³ × 3

36 = 2² × 3²

Answer: HCF 12, LCM 72

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
1 is prime1 has only one factor.
A composite factor left inKeep breaking down until every factor is prime.
HCF or LCM?HCF ≤ the smaller number; LCM ≥ the bigger one.

items.e: 9 is not prime: 9 = 3 × 3, so it has more than two factors.

items.q: Write 63 as a product of prime factors in index form.
items.e: Divide by primes: 3 appears 2 times, 7 appears 1 time. So 63 = 32 × 7.

Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 98 and 42.
items.e: Factors of 98: 1, 2, 7, 14, 49, 98. Factors of 42: 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42. The biggest number in both lists is 14.

items.q: Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 16 and 12.
items.e: Multiples of 16: 16, 32, 48, … The first one that is also a multiple of 12 is 48. (16 × 12 = 192 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.)
